summary:
Escape Protocol: The Hive is an immersive, science-based survival and strategy game designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Players navigate complex maze-like planetary and lunar habitats—ranging from Moon and Mars outposts to icy Europa and stormy Venus—while managing vital life support systems including oxygen, water, power grids, and radiation shielding.  
The core gameplay centers on strategic trade-offs. As players explore the mazes to recover scattered rocket parts and power crystals, they must constantly balance engineering decisions at terminal stations, weighing resource scarcity, environmental hazards like solar radiation flares, and equipment repairs against the clock. Featuring multiple difficulty missions with distinct environmental challenges, plus an asymmetrical "Hunt Mode" where players can experience the game as an alien tracker, Escape Protocol: The Hive transforms aerospace engineering and deep-space survival constraints into a tense, interactive challenge.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Escape Protocol: The Hive is a browser-based STEM survival and strategy game. Players explore habitat mazes across the Moon, Mars, Europa, and Venus to collect scattered rocket parts and reach the launch pad while managing four critical systems: Oxygen, Water, Life Support, and Power Grid. Along the way, players use Hydroponics Bays, Solar Arrays, Sabatier Scrubbers, and Regolith Shields, making engineering trade-offs at terminals where every choice balances power, resources, and radiation protection. An asymmetrical Hunt Mode also lets players act as an alien tracker stopping a human from escaping.

Benefits & Impact
The game turns complex space life-support engineering into interactive gameplay, helping students understand how planetary hazards—like Mars radiation flares, Europa's cold, and Venus's heat—impact deep-space survival.
Creativity & Design
Each world features custom resource drain rates and hazards, supported by cross-platform touch and keyboard controls (WASD, ability hotkeys, and emergency repair) so it plays smoothly on both tablets and desktops.

Tools & Technologies Used
Built using HTML and JavaScript as a lightweight web application, developed and tested on a tablet with AI assistance for coding, debugging, and game-balance tuning.
